name: Jonathan Jackson
bio: Jonathan Jackson has represented Illinois's 1st congressional district since 2023 and sits on the Agriculture and Foreign Affairs committees. Before Congress he was national spokesman for the Rainbow/PUSH Coalition, a financial analyst, a beer-distributorship partner and a business professor at Chicago State University. He was born and raised in Chicago.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All to provide universal health coverage.
Backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and broader voter-access legislation.
Endorses the Women's Health Protection Act to safeguard abortion access.
Wants more funding for under-resourced schools and expanded early childhood education.
Calls for raising wages for working women and ensuring pay equity.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher wages and pay equity for working women and ran as a progressive endorsed by Bernie Sanders.

welfare.evidence: Campaign site lists Medicare for All as a core issue.

liberty.evidence: Supports the Women's Health Protection Act on abortion (choice) while saying more guns must be taken off the streets (restriction).

energy.evidence: Has said climate change is real and a crisis affecting everyone.

education.evidence: Organized opposition to Chicago public school closures and privatization and seeks more funding for under-resourced schools.

notes: Wikipedia lists jacksonforcongress.com as the campaign site; jonathanjacksonforcongress.com appears to be an unaffiliated biography page.

name: Christian Maxwell
bio: Christian Maxwell is an e-commerce growth marketing consultant and entrepreneur from Chicago who won the 2026 Republican nomination in Illinois's 1st district. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois Chicago and has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Names low childhood literacy as a top district concern and supports school choice.
Wants to reduce the tax burden on families and businesses in the district.
Supports empowering law enforcement to address property crime.
Proposes stronger livestock disease response and agricultural biosecurity to stabilize food prices.
Supports immigration policies with health screening, local coordination and transparency with affected communities.
Favors a strategic relationship with China, domestic manufacturing resilience and stronger Taiwan defense.

economy.evidence: Emphasizes lowering taxes on families and businesses and says Chicago and Illinois have a spending problem.

security.evidence: Lists property crime as a top concern and supports empowering law enforcement.

foreign.evidence: Supports strengthening Taiwan's defense capabilities through deterrence and diplomacy.

education.evidence: Supports school choice to address low childhood literacy.

notes: The Sun-Times questionnaire lists unitecd1.com as her campaign site while Wikipedia lists christianmaxwellforcongress.com; the latter's content did not load without JavaScript.

name: Donna Miller
bio: Donna Miller has served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners for the 6th district since 2018 and chairs its veterans committee. She previously worked for decades as a healthcare and biotech consultant and chaired the board of Planned Parenthood of Illinois. A Chicago native and Howard University graduate, she won the 2026 Democratic nomination in Illinois's 2nd district.

platform.point: Supports a Medicare for All framework, insulin price caps and cheaper prescription drugs.
Wants to codify Roe v. Wade and fund maternal health programs.
Would repeal tax breaks for billionaires, back unions and invest in affordable housing.
Backs strong federal AI regulation, child-safety rules for chatbots and state authority to regulate AI.
Supports rejoining the Paris Climate Agreement and investing in clean air and water.
Supports a swift path to citizenship and accountability for agencies that violate civil rights.

economy.evidence: Pledges to repeal tax breaks for billionaires, stand with unions and fund affordable housing.

welfare.evidence: States support for a Medicare for All framework and expanding Medicare and Medicaid.

liberty.evidence: Wants to codify Roe v. Wade (abortion choice) and pass stricter gun laws (guns).

immigration.evidence: Supports a swift, humane path to citizenship and due process for all migrants.

energy.evidence: Supports rejoining the Paris Agreement and cites $100 million in county sustainability investments.

tech.evidence: Calls for strong federal AI regulation, child-safety rules and state authority to regulate AI.

photo.file: File:Donna Miller in front of Christmas Tree.jpg
photo.author: MaylenePena

name: Michael Noack
bio: Michael (Mike) Noack is a truck driver from Bonfield in Kankakee County, where he has lived for 32 years. He has not held elected office and is the 2026 Republican nominee in Illinois's 2nd district.

platform.point: Would convert health insurance companies into nonprofits while opposing government-run healthcare.
Favors investing in hydroelectric power and questions the environmental footprint of wind and solar.
Wants to secure the border, focus ICE on violent criminals and fix the legal immigration process.
Seeks lower property taxes, reversal of Illinois's gas tax increase and cuts to federal spending.
Proposes job pipelines placing veterans in police, airport security and shipyard roles.

economy.evidence: Calls for tax cuts and reduced spending but also wants health insurers converted to nonprofits.

welfare.evidence: Rejects government-run healthcare, preferring a nonprofit private insurance model.

immigration.evidence: Backs border security while opposing ICE targeting of non-dangerous people and supporting legal immigration.

energy.evidence: Criticizes wind and solar as greenwashing while supporting hydroelectric and clean-energy research.

notes: Campaign materials use the name Mike Noack; the ballot listing is Michael Noack.

name: Delia Ramirez
bio: Delia Ramirez has represented Illinois's 3rd congressional district since 2023 and serves on the Homeland Security and Veterans' Affairs committees. She previously served in the Illinois House from 2018 to 2023 and led homelessness and housing nonprofits. She was born in Chicago and raised in Humboldt Park.

platform.point: Co-sponsors the Medicare for All Act for a single-payer system.
Seeks a pathway to citizenship for undocumented people and an end to deportations that separate families.
Co-sponsored a $17 federal minimum wage and the PRO Act; supports a federal jobs guarantee.
Wants more affordable housing and stronger protections for renters against corporate landlords.
Introduced the Melt ICE Act to end DHS funding for immigrant detention and monitoring.

economy.evidence: Co-sponsored the $17 minimum wage and PRO Act and supports a federal jobs guarantee.

welfare.evidence: Co-sponsors the Medicare for All Act for single-payer coverage.

liberty.evidence: Campaign platform supports reproductive rights and LGBTQ+ rights; member of the Congressional Equality Caucus.

immigration.evidence: Introduced the Melt ICE Act to end detention funding and advocates ending deportations.

foreign.evidence: Voted to withdraw U.S. troops from Syria and against several pro-Israel resolutions.

name: Angel Oakley
bio: Angel Oakley owns a marketing and communications firm and is a former Winfield village official. She has been active in Chicago's western suburbs for over 30 years and holds degrees from Judson University. She was a write-in candidate for this district in 2024.

platform.point: Wants oversight, performance reporting and audits for all House-allocated funds and stronger whistleblower protections.
Plans to cut red tape for small businesses, lower taxes on working families and support domestic manufacturing.
Supports a national voter ID standard, a ban on dark money and a digital civic engagement platform.
Favors more parental involvement in curriculum and limits on federal involvement in local schools.
Seeks a clear AI legal framework, stronger data privacy and limits on government surveillance.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting red tape and taxes on working families while supporting fair trade and domestic manufacturing.

welfare.evidence: Would uphold Social Security and Medicare with reforms and favors competition and medical freedom in healthcare.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to defend free speech, religious freedom and Second Amendment rights (speech, guns).

security.evidence: Supports strong policing while opposing mass government surveillance and protecting privacy.

immigration.evidence: Supports stronger border security against illegal entry alongside humane enforcement and immigration reform.

foreign.evidence: Backs a strong military and strategic alliances while avoiding endless wars.

tech.evidence: Wants a clear AI legal framework and child online protections but warns against excessive regulation.

education.evidence: Favors parental involvement in curriculum and limiting federal overreach in local schools.

notes: Wikipedia describes her as a cannabis business consultant, while her campaign site describes a marketing firm.

name: Patty Garcia
current_role: Chief of staff to U.S. Rep. Chuy García
bio: Patty Garcia served as district director and then chief of staff for U.S. Representative Chuy García in Illinois's 4th district. She holds a Ph.D. in education policy from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and has worked with immigrant and working-class communities for over 15 years. She was the only candidate on the 2026 Democratic primary ballot after García withdrew.

platform.point: Supports a higher federal minimum wage, the PRO Act, an expanded Child Tax Credit and penalties for price gouging.
Backs Medicare for All and Medicare drug price negotiation.
Supports a pathway to citizenship, protections for Dreamers and abolishing ICE.
Wants more federal public school funding, higher teacher pay, larger Pell Grants and student debt relief.
Calls for a permanent Gaza ceasefire and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.
Supports expanding clean energy, public transit and lead pipe replacement.

economy.evidence: Wants the rich to pay more, a higher minimum wage, the PRO Act and penalties for companies raising essential prices.

welfare.evidence: Backs Medicare for All and an expanded Child Tax Credit.

immigration.evidence: Supports a pathway to citizenship and abolishing ICE.

foreign.evidence: Favors diplomacy over military force, more congressional war-powers control and ending arms shipments to Israel.

energy.evidence: Advocates a strong push to a clean energy economy.

education.evidence: Opposes privatizing public schools and wants more federal public school funding.

photo.file: File:Patty Garcia with Alderman Andre Vasquez at Fundraiser Cropped.jpg
photo.author: Paul Goyette

name: Lupe Castillo
bio: Lupe Castillo is a pharmacy technician and the 2026 Republican nominee in Illinois's 4th district. Castillo also ran for this seat in 2024.
notes: No campaign website or issue statements were found; Ballotpedia pages could not be loaded.

name: Chris Getty
bio: Chris Getty is the mayor of the Village of Lyons and previously served as Lyons Township supervisor and on the township mental health board. He is a licensed insurance producer and a graduate of Eastern Illinois University. Born and raised in Lyons, he is a registered Democrat running as an independent.

platform.point: Lists cost of living as a top campaign priority.
Says he will advocate for responsible immigration solutions and public safety.
Pledges to restore trust in government and protect election integrity.

notes: Campaign site lists priorities without specific proposals, so no positions were scored.

name: Ed Hershey
bio: Ed Hershey teaches at Lindblom High School on Chicago's South Side, where he has served as a union representative. Born in Rochester, New York, and a University of Chicago graduate, he ran for 25th Ward alderman in 2015 and was the Working Class Party nominee for this seat in 2022 and 2024.

platform.point: Proposes automatic wage increases tied to inflation and work-sharing to create jobs.
Would tax wealthy individuals and corporations to reduce the deficit.
Supports full rights, including voting rights, for all immigrants and federal funding to house asylum seekers.
Opposes U.S. military aid to Israel and U.S. involvement in Ukraine.
Aims to build an independent working-class political party separate from Democrats and Republicans.

economy.evidence: Calls for taxing the wealthy and corporations, inflation-indexed wages and redirecting profits to workers.

immigration.evidence: Supports immediate full rights, including voting, for all immigrants.

foreign.evidence: Opposes military aid to Israel and U.S. support for Ukraine.

notes: Positions come from his 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire; no 2026-specific platform was found. The website is the Working Class Party's site, not a personal campaign site.

name: Mike Quigley
bio: Mike Quigley has represented Illinois's 5th congressional district since a 2009 special election. He previously served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners from 1998 to 2009 and taught environmental policy at Loyola University Chicago. Raised in Carol Stream, he has lived in Chicago's Lakeview area since 1982.

platform.point: Focuses on government reform, transparency and anti-corruption measures.
Supports full LGBTQ equality under the law.
Pushes strong environmental policies to address climate change.
Backs background checks on every firearm sale and limits on large-capacity ammunition.
Advocates infrastructure investment to create well-paying jobs.
Voted against a 2023 funding bill because it lacked aid to Ukraine.

welfare.evidence: Announced support for the Medicare for All Act of 2021.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and LGBTQ equality (choice) and universal background checks and ammunition limits (guns).

security.evidence: Voted to extend PATRIOT Act roving wiretaps and for cybersecurity data-sharing with government.

immigration.evidence: Voted to legalize Dreamers via military service and sponsored a bill barring religion-based immigration bans.

foreign.evidence: Was the only Democrat to oppose a 2023 funding bill lacking Ukraine aid and backed 2024 Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan aid.

energy.evidence: Voted for the 2009 cap-and-trade bill and against barring EPA regulation of greenhouse gases.

tech.evidence: Sponsored a bill to restore net neutrality.

notes: Wikipedia reports he is also running for mayor of Chicago in 2027.

name: Tommy Hanson
bio: Tommy Hanson is a self-employed commercial real estate broker who grew up in Chicago's north suburbs. He earlier sold advertising for the Chicago Tribune and U.S. News & World Report. He has run for office several times and is the 2026 Republican nominee in Illinois's 5th district.

platform.point: Proposes replacing individual income taxes with corporate taxes, tariffs and a Fair Tax.
Wants no taxes on food or gasoline and lower property, electricity and phone costs.
Wants violent offenders kept in jail without early release and full support for law enforcement.
Would let each state decide whether ICE operates within its borders.
Seeks to cut federal spending and debt and limit federal power under the Tenth Amendment.
Wants simpler CHA housing vouchers and help for first-time homebuyers.

economy.evidence: Seeks fewer regulations and taxes on businesses, federal spending cuts and free-market competition.

liberty.evidence: Says he is pro-life (abortion); his campaign homepage separately calls him socially liberal and proposes using federal marijuana tax revenue for road repairs (drugs).

security.evidence: Calls for no early release or reduced bail for violent criminals and full law-enforcement funding.

immigration.evidence: Backs strong lawful immigration levels while calling for a secured southern border and action against illegal immigration.

notes: Campaign site content dates partly from his 2022 run.
